headline: Japanese Fireworks Now Dissolve in Water, Eliminating Debris
meta_description: A Japanese university professor and fireworks company have created water-soluble shells that dissolve harmlessly in the environment, eliminating cleanup after…
summary_short: A fireworks company and university professor have partnered to create the world's first water-soluble fireworks shells, using a resin already approved for agricultural u…
body:
When Ryukoku University professor Takahiko Nakaoki and Hiroyuki Kakinoki, president of Kakinoki Fireworks Industry Co., joined forces, they solved a problem that had frustrated the fireworks industry for years. Together, they developed what may be the world's first water-soluble fireworks shells and canisters—a breakthrough that promises to eliminate the debris scattered across cities after holiday celebrations. Rather than inventing an entirely new material, the innovation uses a water-soluble resin already approved for agricultural seeds and soil improvers. When exposed to moisture, the shell becomes soft and sloughy like hot caramel, allowing it to dissolve harmlessly into the ecosystem without leaving a trace for street-sweepers to clean up.

Mr. Kakinoki had been pursuing this vision since at least 2018, when he first met Professor Nakaoki. His earlier attempts to develop eco-friendly shells using resins had repeatedly failed, forcing him to abandon the effort—until the professor's insight changed everything. The timing is practical: many Japanese fireworks displays occur near water bodies like large rivers, lakes, and the ocean, meaning most water-soluble casings will vanish within hours of a show.

The environmental gains extend beyond the shells themselves. Kraft paper is used during packaging and storage to keep moisture away from the shell, but the new eco-friendly fireworks require about half as much paper as conventional ones. This year, Kakinoki Fireworks plans to produce 20,000 fireworks total, with President Kakinoki hoping that 10,000 of them will be these environmentally friendly versions—a meaningful commitment to reducing the ecological footprint of celebration.
quick_facts: Water-soluble shells dissolve in hours near water bodies
Uses agricultural resin already approved for environmental safety
Reduces packaging paper use by approximately 50 percent
Partnership began in 2018 after earlier resin experiments failed
10,000 of 20,000 planned fireworks this year to be eco-friendly
